      corporate:  compliance, finance, workforce, procurement, masterdata

    the current division assignment of every existing domain is unchanged, and any new domain
    must be classified into exactly one of these three.
  - Preserve the accurate maritime terminology and structures the reviewer called correct:
    TEU/FEU, LoLo/RoRo, MARSEC, ISPS, MARPOL, SOLAS, VGM, IMDG, BAPLIE, NAVIS N4 / TOPS Expert,
    the deep tariff/billing structure, and the well-formed marine-services tables. Do NOT regress them.
  - Preserve the five ECM-only enterprise domains the reviewer credited for closing MVM gaps:
    workforce (labor/stevedoring), asset (equipment M&R), contract, procurement, safety (HSE).

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 1 - add_product: cargo.transhipment - model transhipment (T/S) as a FIRST-CLASS concept, not a generic container visit. Add product cargo.transhipment (a T/S move that links an inbound vessel call to an outbound vessel call, with connection window, T/S dwell time, relay vs feeder classification) plus cargo.transhipment_leg. Reviewer: "Transhipment as a first-class concept - T/S is 50%+ of volume at hub ports like Jebel Ali, Khalifa, Salalah, Singapore. Currently treated as a generic container visit." FK the transhipment to the existing inbound/outbound vessel.call and cargo.container.

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 2 - add_product: cargo.empty_container_pool - add empty container / MTY pool / depot operations. Add products cargo.empty_container_pool (MTY pool balance by depot/type), cargo.container_depot (off-dock/on-dock depot facility), cargo.container_lease (leasing agreement + per-diem), and cargo.depot_repair_order (M&R work order for empties). Reviewer: "Empty container / depot operations - MTY pool tracking, container leasing, repair work orders."

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 3 - add_product: masterdata.edi_message_type - build out EDI / Port Community System message tracking. Add reference product masterdata.edi_message_type enumerating the real PCS message standards (COPARN, COPRAR, COARRI, CODECO, BAPLIE, IFTMIN, MOVINS, CUSCAR, CUSRES, VERMAS), and add product cargo.pcs_message (a Port Community System message-event log for the container/cargo lifecycle, FK to masterdata.edi_partner and masterdata.edi_message_type, modeling DP World CONNECT and Mirsal 2 exchanges). Reviewer: "EDI / Port Community System - masterdata.edi_partner is there but no message tracking. Real ports run on COPARN, COPRAR, COARRI, CODECO, BAPLIE, IFTMIN, MOVINS, CUSCAR. In Dubai specifically, integration with DP World CONNECT and Mirsal 2 is the PCS backbone."

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 4 - add_domain: sustainability - create a new FIRST-CLASS domain sustainability in the operations division for decarbonization tracking, with products cii_rating (IMO Carbon Intensity Indicator A-E rating per vessel/year), eexi_record (Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index), shore_power_session (cold-ironing / OPS session with kWh and emissions avoided), and bunker_carbon_intensity (well-to-wake carbon intensity of bunkered fuel). Reviewer: "Sustainability / decarbonization - CII (Carbon Intensity Indicator), EEXI, shore power, bunker carbon intensity. IMO 2030/2050 is the strategic agenda for ports through 2030." Classify sustainability as division=operations; FK to masterdata.vessel_master and vessel.call where relevant.

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 5 - add_product: compliance.free_trade_zone - add Free Trade Zone / FZC constructs. Add products compliance.free_trade_zone (FTZ/FZC registry: JAFZA, KIZAD, Singapore, HK, Panama), cargo.ftz_bonded_cargo (bonded cargo held under FTZ customs suspension), and compliance.ftz_customs_treatment (FTZ customs regime/entry treatment). Reviewer: "Free Trade Zone constructs - FZC, FTZ-bonded cargo, FTZ customs treatment. Relevant for JAFZA, KIZAD, Singapore, HK, Panama."

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 6 - add_product: vessel.disbursement_account - flesh out the vessel agency disbursement (DA) workflow. Add products vessel.disbursement_account (final DA statement), vessel.proforma_disbursement (pro-forma DA estimate), vessel.husbandry_service (husbandry services rendered to the vessel), and vessel.crew_change (crew change event coordinated by the agent). FK them to the existing vessel.agency_appointment. Reviewer: "Vessel agency disbursement workflow - agent_appointment exists but DA, pro-forma DA, husbandry services, crew change would round it out."

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 7 - add_product: terminal.rehandling_event - model rehandling / restow / pull-and-replace as first-class events. Add products terminal.rehandling_event (yard rehandle / pull-and-replace of a container to reach another) and terminal.restow_event (on-board restow move). Reviewer: "Rehandling / restow / pull-and-replace events - a hidden but significant cost driver." FK to cargo.container and the relevant terminal yard/vessel-stow position.

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 8 - add_product: cargo.dg_segregation_rule - add dangerous-goods (DG) segregation logic on top of the existing imdg_class and dangerous_goods_declaration. Add products cargo.dg_segregation_rule (IMDG segregation matrix rule between two IMDG classes) and cargo.dg_positioning_constraint (vessel/yard positioning constraint for a DG unit). Reviewer: "DG segregation logic - imdg_class and dangerous_goods_declaration are there, but no segregation rule engine or DG positioning constraints on vessel/yard."

REVIEWER-PRIORITY 9 - add_product: cargo.container_condition_report - complete the container damage / claims workflow around the existing cargo.damage_claim. Add products cargo.container_condition_report (EIR / condition survey at gate/interchange) and cargo.damage_liability (liability apportionment for a damage claim). FK cargo.damage_liability to the existing cargo.damage_claim; do NOT duplicate the claim table. Reviewer: "Container damage / claims - condition reports, damage liability, insurance claim workflow."

after.description: SSOT for the physical deployment and transfer history of each port asset within the terminal footprint. Records every location assignment and inter-zone transfer as a time-stamped event, capturing assigned berth, quay zone, yard block, terminal area, or maintenance bay, along with location code, terminal zone, GPS coordinates, effective assignment date, transfer reason, authorising officer, originating and destination cost centres, and operational area designation. Subsumes all asset relocation and transfer tracking. Supports yard planning, equipment dispatch, maintenance crew routing, and cost centre reallocation. Integrates with NAVIS N4 and TOPS Expert for real-time equipment positioning.

Annual or periodic procurement plan defining anticipated purchasing requirements aligned to port operational and capital budgets. Captures plan period, total planned spend by material group and department, sourcing strategy per category (open market, preferred vendor, competitive tender), planned tender schedule, approval workflow requirements by value threshold, and alignment to CAPEX/OPEX budgets. Supports procurement pipeline management, budget commitment planning, and governance compliance.

after.description: Reference to the employee designated as the asset manager responsible for the lifecycle management of this asset post-acquisition. Links to workforce employee master data.

Level of access control required for personnel and equipment entering this location. Public for unrestricted areas; authorized for credentialed staff; escort required for visitor areas; permit only for special authorization zones; emergency only for restricted emergency access.

Unique identifier for each asset location assignment record. Primary key. Inferred role: TRANSACTION_HEADER (each location assignment is a discrete business event with lifecycle). This entity tracks location assignment events for port assets.
Externally-known business identifier for this location assignment event. Used for tracking and audit purposes across NAVIS N4 and TOPS Expert systems.

Business priority level for this location assignment. Critical for emergency response or safety-critical equipment; high for revenue-generating operations; medium for routine redeployment; low for optimization or non-urgent transfers.

Current lifecycle state of the location assignment. Active indicates the asset is currently deployed at this location; pending indicates scheduled future assignment; completed indicates historical assignment; cancelled indicates assignment was revoked; suspended indicates temporary hold.
Precise date and time when the location assignment was executed or recorded in the Terminal Operating System (TOS). Principal business event timestamp for this location assignment transaction.
Name or identifier of the port authority officer, terminal manager, or operations supervisor who approved the asset location assignment or transfer. Used for accountability and audit trail.
Identifier for the specific berth where the asset is assigned, if applicable. Relevant for quayside equipment such as Ship-to-Shore (STS) cranes and Quay Cranes (QC). Null for non-berth locations.
Date and time when this asset location assignment record was first created in the system. Audit trail timestamp for record creation.

Financial cost centre code to which the asset is being assigned. Used for inter-departmental cost allocation and Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) / Operational Expenditure (OPEX) tracking in SAP S/4HANA Controlling (CO) module.
Reference number of the equipment dispatch order that initiated this location assignment. Links to NAVIS N4 or TOPS Expert dispatch management for operational coordination.
Physical distance in meters between the previous location and current location. Used for transfer cost estimation, fuel consumption tracking, and logistics planning.
Date when the asset location assignment becomes effective. Marks the start of the assets deployment at this location. Used for historical tracking and yard planning.
Date when the asset location assignment ends or is scheduled to end. Null for current active assignments. Used for transfer planning and historical analysis.

Environmental classification of the location area. Standard for normal operations; controlled emission for Greenhouse Gas (GHG) monitoring zones; noise restricted for residential proximity; hazmat for International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) handling; marine protected for environmentally sensitive areas per Marine Pollution Convention (MARPOL).

Geographic latitude coordinate of the asset location in decimal degrees. Supports real-time equipment positioning and dispatch routing. Integrates with Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS) and Terminal Operating System (TOS).

Geographic longitude coordinate of the asset location in decimal degrees. Supports real-time equipment positioning and dispatch routing. Integrates with Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS) and Terminal Operating System (TOS).
Flag indicating whether this location assignment is temporary (True) or permanent (False). Temporary assignments are typically for short-term operational needs, maintenance, or project work.
Date and time when this asset location assignment record was most recently modified. Audit trail timestamp for record updates.

Maximum load bearing capacity of the location surface in metric tonnes. Critical for ensuring Safe Working Load (SWL) compliance when deploying heavy equipment such as Mobile Harbour Cranes (MHC), Rubber Tyred Gantry (RTG) cranes, or loaded vehicles.

Standardized alphanumeric code identifying the specific physical location within the terminal footprint. May represent berth, quay zone, yard block, Container Yard (CY), maintenance bay, or equipment staging area.
Human-readable name or description of the physical location where the asset is deployed. Examples: Berth 5 North, Yard Block A3, Maintenance Bay 2, Quay Crane Rail 7.

Flag indicating whether data network connectivity (wired or wireless) is available at this location (True) or not (False). Required for Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tracking, Terminal Operating System (TOS) integration, and real-time equipment monitoring.
Location code where the asset is scheduled to be transferred next. Null if no future transfer is planned. Supports forward planning and equipment dispatch optimization.

Free-text field for additional comments, special instructions, operational notes, or contextual information related to this asset location assignment. Used for communication between operations, maintenance, and planning teams.

Functional designation of the operational area where the asset is deployed. Container terminal for Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit (TEU) / Forty-foot Equivalent Unit (FEU) handling; bulk cargo for dry/liquid bulk; Roll-on Roll-off (RoRo) for vehicle shipping; general cargo for break-bulk; intermodal for rail/road transfer; maintenance depot for repair facilities; administration for support functions. Financial cost centre code from which the asset is being transferred. Used for inter-departmental cost allocation and Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) / Operational Expenditure (OPEX) tracking in SAP S/4HANA Controlling (CO) module.

Reference to the port asset being located or transferred. Links to the asset registry for equipment such as Ship-to-Shore (STS) cranes, Rubber Tyred Gantry (RTG) cranes, Automated Stacking Cranes (ASC), Automated Guided Vehicles (AGV), Mobile Harbour Cranes (MHC), forklifts, and port vehicles.

Flag indicating whether electrical power supply infrastructure is available at this location (True) or not (False). Relevant for electrically-powered equipment such as Ship-to-Shore (STS) cranes, Automated Stacking Cranes (ASC), and charging stations for Automated Guided Vehicles (AGV).
Location code where the asset was deployed immediately prior to this assignment. Null for initial deployment. Supports transfer history tracking and equipment movement analysis.

Safety and security classification of the location area. Unrestricted for general access; restricted for authorized personnel only; hazardous for dangerous goods areas; International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) controlled for security zones; confined space for Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) regulated areas.

Physical surface type of the location area. Concrete for paved quay and yard; asphalt for roadways; gravel for unpaved areas; rail for rail-mounted equipment zones; water for floating equipment; mixed for composite surfaces. Relevant for equipment compatibility and Safe Working Load (SWL) considerations.

High-level operational area designation within the port terminal. Quayside for berth and crane operations; yard for container stacking; gate for entry/exit; maintenance for repair facilities; intermodal for rail/road transfer; storage for warehousing; administration for office areas. Detailed narrative explanation of the location assignment or transfer, including context, operational requirements, and any special instructions for equipment dispatch or maintenance crew routing.
Actual or estimated time in hours required to physically relocate the asset from the previous location to the current location. Includes mobilization, transit, and positioning time.

Business justification for the asset location assignment or transfer. before.description: Batch billing execution records capturing each scheduled or ad-hoc billing cycle run that generates invoices from NAVIS N4 TOS charge data. Captures billing run reference, run type (periodic/vessel-call/ad-hoc/final), billing period start and end dates, run date and time, total invoices generated, total invoice value, currency, run status (scheduled/in-progress/completed/failed/cancelled), operator ID, NAVIS N4 export batch reference, and SAP posting batch reference. Provides full audit trail of invoice generation cycles.
Indicates whether this billing run requires manual approval before invoices are released to customers. True for high-value or adjustment runs; false for routine periodic runs.
Date and time when the billing run was approved for invoice release. Null if approval is not required or not yet granted.

Foreign key linking to billing.billing_cycle. Business justification: Each billing run executes for a specific billing cycle. The billing_cycle table defines the authoritative billing period. Adding billing_cycle_id allows JOIN to retrieve cycle configuration and remove
Source system from which billing charges were extracted: NAVIS-N4 (primary TOS), TOPS-EXPERT (alternate TOS), MANUAL (manual entry), or PCS (Port Community System for customs/trade charges).
Date and time when this billing run record was first created in the system. Represents the initial scheduling or setup of the billing run.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the total invoice value (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). All invoices in a single run use the same base currency.
Total elapsed time in seconds from run start to run end. Used for performance monitoring and capacity planning of billing batch jobs.
Date and time when the billing run execution completed or terminated. Null if run is still in-progress or suspended.
Number of errors or exceptions encountered during billing run execution. Zero indicates a clean run; non-zero requires review of error logs.
High-level summary description of errors encountered during the billing run. Null if no errors occurred. Detailed error logs are maintained separately.
Date on which the billing run revenue was posted to the General Ledger in SAP S/4HANA FI. Null if GL posting has not yet occurred.
Date and time when invoices from this billing run were released and made available to customers via EDI, email, or customer portal. Null if not yet released.
Date and time when this billing run record was last updated. Tracks any changes to status, approval, or other attributes throughout the run lifecycle.
Reference identifier of the NAVIS N4 TOS charge export batch that sourced the billing data for this run. Provides traceability back to the Terminal Operating System.
Free-text notes or comments entered by billing operators regarding special circumstances, manual adjustments, or issues encountered during the billing run execution.
Externally-known unique reference number for the billing run, formatted as BR-YYYYMMDD-NNNN for traceability and audit purposes.
Reference to the original billing run ID if this run is a rerun or correction of a previous failed or cancelled run. Null for original runs.
Accounting period (YYYY-MM format) to which revenue from this billing run is recognized for financial reporting and EBITDA calculation purposes.
User identifier of the finance manager or authorized approver who approved the billing run for release. Null if approval is not required or not yet granted.
User identifier or system account that initiated or executed the billing run. For scheduled runs, this may be a system service account; for ad-hoc runs, this is the manual operator.
Unique identifier for the billing run batch execution record. Primary key.

Current lifecycle status of the billing run: scheduled (queued for execution), in-progress (actively processing), completed (successfully finished), failed (error encountered), cancelled (manually aborted), or suspended (paused pending resolution).

Classification of the billing run execution type: periodic (scheduled monthly/weekly), vessel-call (per vessel departure), ad-hoc (manual trigger), final (end-of-period close), adjustment (correction run), or reversal (cancellation run).
Reference identifier of the SAP S/4HANA FI posting batch where generated invoices were posted for financial accounting. Null if posting has not yet occurred or failed.
Date on which this billing run was originally scheduled to execute. May differ from actual run start date if the run was delayed or rescheduled.
Date and time when the billing run execution began processing charges from NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System (TOS). Represents the actual start of the batch job.
Total number of individual charge line items processed and aggregated into invoices during this billing run.
Distinct count of customer accounts that received at least one invoice in this billing run.
Aggregate monetary value of all invoices generated in this billing run, representing gross revenue before adjustments. Used for EBITDA-level revenue reporting.

after.description: Batch billing execution records capturing each scheduled or ad-hoc billing cycle run that generates invoices from NAVIS N4 TOS charge data. Captures billing run reference, run type (periodic/vessel-call/ad-hoc/final), billing period start and end dates, run date and time, total invoices generated, total invoice value, currency, run status (scheduled/in-progress/completed/failed/cancelled), operator ID, NAVIS N4 export batch reference, and SAP posting batch reference. Provides full audit trail of invoice generation cycles.
Master reference table for terminal. Referenced by terminal_id.

Master catalog of intermodal transport services and corridors offered by the port, including rail shuttle services, ICD linkage routes, drayage service packages, and scheduled inland connections. Captures service code, name, transport mode, origin-destination corridor, route distance (km), transit time benchmark, frequency, capacity (TEU), active operators, tariff reference, and service status. SSOT for intermodal service offerings and corridor definitions.

Transactional record representing a single transport leg within a multimodal journey, capturing leg sequence number, transport mode (sea, rail, road, barge), carrier, origin node, destination node, scheduled and actual departure/arrival, distance (km), and leg status. Enables end-to-end multimodal journey decomposition and tracking.

Regulatory filing and gazette publication record for port tariff schedules. Captures the submission to the port regulator or maritime authority, filing reference number, gazette publication date, public comment period, approval status, conditions imposed, and effective date granted. Tracks the full regulatory lifecycle from draft submission through public consultation to final approval. Required for compliance with port pricing regulations and enables audit of tariff legitimacy.

Version control record for port tariff schedules, capturing the full history of tariff revisions, amendments, and regulatory approvals. Each record represents a specific version of a tariff schedule with its publication date, effective date, superseded date, change summary, regulatory filing reference, approval authority, and publication channel (gazette, EDI, PCS). Enables full tariff audit trail and supports retroactive billing corrections.
